title: Card Services Basis Note: Authorizing Charges and Pricing Them on Personal Credit Cards
content:
**Authorization of purchases.** Purchases on Personal Credit Cards are authorized only on an active account and only while the balance after the purchase stays within the credit limit increased by the tier's over-limit tolerance percentage. No over-limit fee is ever charged. Charges post only to an account whose status is active; the status is read from the bank's card record for that account before the charge posts, and purchases, cash advances and balance transfers alike are held to it.

**Cash advances.** Cash advances posted in a statement cycle, being the amounts of the cash advances posted in the current statement cycle added together, may not exceed the tier's cash advance share of the credit limit. Each cash advance incurs a cash advance fee equal to the greater of two figures: the tier's cash advance percentage of the advance, rounded half-up to the cent, and the tier's smallest cash advance fee.

**Balance transfers.** Balance transfers are accepted only on a tier that allows them. Each incurs a fee equal to the greater of the tier's transfer percentage of the transfer, rounded half-up to the cent, and the tier's smallest transfer fee. A balance transfer posted within the tier's window of calendar days after opening carries the introductory rate until the introductory rate end date; one posted later carries the purchase rate.

**Purchases made abroad.** A purchase marked as a foreign transaction incurs the tier's foreign transaction percentage of its amount, rounded half-up to the cent, billed as a foreign transaction fee. A tier percentage of 0.00 writes no entry at all.

**How a transaction fee is tied to its transaction.** A transaction fee carries the transaction it prices as its source item and the same statement cycle as that transaction.

**Rewards.** Cash advances and balance transfers never earn rewards.

*Worked illustrations on hypothetical figures.* On a tier pricing cash advances at 5.0 percent with a floor of 10.00 USD, an advance of 400.00 USD yields 20.00 USD by the percentage, which is the greater of the two, so 20.00 USD is billed; an advance of 150.00 USD yields 7.50 USD by the percentage, so the floor of 10.00 USD is billed instead. On a tier pricing transfers at 3.0 percent with a floor of 5.00 USD, a transfer of 100.00 USD yields 3.00 USD by the percentage and the floor of 5.00 USD is billed. A purchase of 250.00 USD marked as a foreign transaction on a tier charging 3.0 percent yields 7.50 USD; on a tier charging 0.0 percent no fee entry is written.
